gen-gf-oxanium-gf-glegoo: Oxanium draws a big-lowercase heading in smooth, unbroken lines with no brush-like swelling. Glegoo, a text serif, is the reverse: tall and generous, with wide curved mouths that stay open.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-hanuman: Commanding up top, traditional below, and the two never blur together. Oxanium keeps every stroke uniform and crisp, while Hanuman sits in a high-waisted lowercase with wide-set terminals on its s.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-kadwa: Kadwa reads classic and editorial, its curves left open and its lowercase larger than usual. And Oxanium's bent-pipe strokes of constant width give that softness something rigid to push against.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noticia-text: Dignified is the mood Noticia Text sets, with its big entrance into each curve. Oxanium, drawn like a ballpoint pen line, supplies the hard edge, and the text serif lowercase fills nearly its whole height.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-piazzolla: Authoritative, from top to bottom. Oxanium traces its glyphs in a single thickness, while Piazzolla, a classic serif, brings lowercase that nearly matches its capitals and an e opened wide.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-scope-one: Scope One reads traditional and refined, its counters spilling into the space around them. But Oxanium's steady, pressure-free line is what makes that classic serif look so soft by comparison.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-suwannaphum: Suwannaphum reads dignified and editorial, with a high, squared-off x-height like woodblock type. Suwannaphum keeps that chunky lowercase and bent-paperclip c going across paragraphs, while Oxanium's constant-width brush-like strokes stay in the heading.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-fauna-one: Fauna One reads literary and dignified, with a tall middle band and shallow ascenders and descenders. Paprika's expressive display letters make a lively contrast.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-glegoo: Scattered, bold, and loud. Glegoo, the classic serif below, feels refined and editorial beside Paprika's wide-spaced, capital-like lowercase, quieter without ever turning timid.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-hanuman: Paprika fills the line with commanding, expressive lowercase that looks almost like capitals. Hanuman, a classic serif with a high-waisted lowercase and wide-set s terminals, would carry a longer passage with a traditional, refined feel.
